decisions.executionNote: Approach yellow nut with left and gray nut with right using a gradual elbow-up lift and downward wrist rotation; initial visual position estimates will be refined.
Finish vertical approach and lower open grippers above the yellow and gray nuts. Keep separate workspaces and check wrist alignment before closing.
Apply small wrist-image centering corrections, close on both nuts, and lift vertically to verify retention visually.
Both nuts appear retained. Raise for bolt clearance, then carry yellow leftward and gray rightward above their matching upright screws.
Center the nut holes laterally over the visible screw shafts, then lower slowly to initial engagement height while retaining both nuts.
Wrist views suggest the shafts remain behind the nut holes. Lift slightly for clearance, correct forward alignment, and approach again cautiously.
Lower the aligned nuts a few millimeters and begin a controlled clockwise tightening stroke with both grippers closed; inspect thread engagement afterward.
The screw tips remain visibly off-axis after the trial turn. Lift clear, restore wrist yaw, and shift the nuts back and outward toward the shaft centers before reattempting insertion.
Use the exposed screw-tip positions in the wrist views to correct lateral and forward centering, then descend slowly without turning.
Both screw tips are now visible within the nut openings. Test engagement with a small clockwise turn and only 3 mm descent, checking whether the axes remain aligned.
The small turn reveals a fore-aft axis offset. Lift clear, restore yaw, shift both nuts 25 mm toward the robot to the screw axes, and approach again.
The wrist response shows the previous fore-aft correction was reversed. Lift clear and move forward past the prior alignment, then lower to check centering without rotation.
The screw tips now appear through the nut openings. Lower gently and test a short clockwise stroke, limiting downward travel while checking for concentric engagement.
The test turn still exposes an axis offset. Lift to avoid scraping, restore yaw, and make a measured forward correction based on the wrist-image response before another engagement attempt.
Move back between the two observed fore-aft positions, make small outward centering corrections, and lower gradually to engage the screw tips with a short test turn.
Lift clear and re-center using the screw bases in the head view rather than apparent overlap in the oblique wrist views. Restore yaw and approach the recalculated axes.
Use the visible screw-tip centers for a small lateral and forward adjustment, then lower carefully with a minimal test turn to check insertion.
Yellow appears centered on its screw; correct the gray nut a few millimeters laterally and apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with limited descent.
Yellow now appears seated around its screw; release and lift to inspect. Gray remains off-axis, so lift it clear, shift toward the visible shaft center, and lower without turning.
Yellow remains seated after release. Move the left arm above the red nut while the right makes a small measured centering adjustment and short engagement turn on gray.
Descend the open left gripper toward the red nut. Make a small gray alignment correction from the remaining visible shaft offset, keeping it clear during translation.
Center and grasp the red nut, then lift to verify retention. Gray's shaft is nearly centered; correct the small residual offset and continue a slow tightening stroke.
Red is retained; carry it above its matching screw with clearance. Refine gray alignment by the remaining small shaft offset, lower gently, and test a minimal tightening turn.

Lower red along its visibly aligned shaft. For gray, make a small clearance-assisted adjustment toward the remaining tip offset and continue a limited clockwise stroke without nearing the wrist limit.
Hold wrist angles fixed to isolate centering. Lift briefly, translate each nut toward the visible screw tip in its wrist image, and return to engagement height without twisting.
The fixed-angle translations moved the screw tips toward the openings. Continue the measured red correction and remove gray's remaining lateral offset, then lower only 2 mm beyond the prior height.
Continue fixed-yaw centering: red's tip remains behind the opening, while gray needs a small leftward image correction. Lower 5 mm after the clearance-assisted shifts, without adding wrist rotation.
Gray's shaft appears centered: apply a short tightening stroke, release, and rewind the open wrist away from its limit. Finish red's small centering correction and test a gentle clockwise stroke.
Gray did not remain on its screw after release. Approach the loose gray nut for a cleaner regrasp; release and lift from red to inspect its actual seating rather than infer engagement from overlap.
Both red and gray are visibly loose. Reset the open wrists to a common vertical approach, above the observed nut positions, to obtain centered grasps before transporting them again.
Center both loose nuts deeper between the fingers with vertical wrists, descend to pickup height, and close gently. Retention and nut orientation will be checked before transport.
Lift red to check retention. Gray appears too far toward the fingertips; reopen, move back slightly for a centered grasp, then close and lift vertically for verification.
Gray is visibly retained in the new centered grasp; raise it above the shaft and carry toward the measured bolt axis. Red was dropped, so approach its new table position with the left gripper open.
Close around the centered red nut without pushing farther past the nearby screw, then lift to verify. Refine gray's fore-aft alignment and descend slowly along the screw axis.
Re-approach red lower and farther back, rotating the open fingers away from the adjacent screw. Apply a small gray lateral correction and short tightening test while keeping its grasp.

Gray is much closer to concentric after the new grasp; make a millimeter correction and continue a slow tightening stroke. Pinch and lift the edge-standing red nut to verify a secure grasp before reorienting it.
Red is securely held on edge; raise it well clear for controlled reorientation. Re-center gray from the head-view shaft axis with a small rightward and rearward translation, without further twisting.

Reorient the edge-held red nut above the table by rotating around its approximate center with compensating EE translation. Make a small clearance-assisted gray correction toward the visible screw-tip offset.

Finish leveling the edge-held red nut, then lower it toward a clear placement area for an upright regrasp. Gray's cap is now laterally centered; correct the small remaining fore-aft offset and descend cautiously.

The rotation guard stopped further left wrist tilting; retain the current nearly level nut orientation and use translation only to lower toward a clear table spot. Resume gray's uncompleted centering correction from the latest pose, then test a very short turn.

Left cannot safely descend farther in this wrist configuration: release the nearly upright red nut over the clear area and retreat upward before restoring the wrist. Gray's tip is now within the opening; apply a slow tightening stroke with minimal descent.

Use much smaller left wrist increments after the continuity rejection while retreating open from red. Gray lost concentricity during turning; hold its angle fixed and correct toward the visible shaft before any further tightening.

Restore the open left wrist toward vertical while lifting, allowing red to clear the fingers. Gray has shifted within the grasp; release and lift to inspect its actual placement before another attempt.
Red has cleared the fingers and appears upright on the table. Restore a vertical left approach above it; lift and unwind the open right wrist to inspect the loose gray nut safely.
Approach the now-upright red nut using its head-view center and a vertical wrist. Descend the open right gripper toward gray, stopping higher because it is resting close to the screw.
Refine both grasps from the wrist views, close around the nuts, and lift a short distance to verify retention and orientation before moving toward the screws.
Both nuts are retained. Carry red above its matching screw with clearance; position gray using the head-view screw axis and descend without turning to check seating before tightening.

Lower red vertically from its clearance height toward the aligned screw. Gray remains visibly behind the hole in the wrist view; hold yaw fixed and make a forward correction before another seating attempt.

Gray's screw cap is now visible within the opening; make a small centering correction and test a short tightening stroke. Lift red clear because its nut appears to have tilted on contact, avoiding further downward pressure.

Red is now visibly seated around its screw after the lift; open and clear the left hand. Keep gray's yaw fixed, correct toward its visible cap, and lower carefully before judging whether it has seated.
Red and yellow remain seated after release. Start returning the left arm safely; center gray by a few millimeters, lower gently onto the shaft, then release and lift to inspect actual seating.
Finish the left arm's return to origin with its gripper open. Gray was not retained on the shaft after release; raise the open right hand and allow the loose nut to settle before replanning.
Keep the left arm at origin. Approach the settled, upright gray nut with the right gripper open, using its head-view center and a straight downward approach for a cleaner grasp.
Center the gray nut between the fingers with a small wrist-image correction, close, and lift vertically above the screw for an unobstructed alignment check.
The gray nut is now centered and upright in the grasp. Carry it above the screw axis estimated from the head view, then descend straight to engagement height without twisting.
The gray shaft appears centered within the nut opening. Lower a few millimeters and apply a controlled clockwise tightening stroke, keeping the left arm clear at origin.
The gray shaft moved off-center during the turn. Keep wrist angle fixed, lift slightly to clear contact, correct toward the visible tip, and lower cautiously before attempting further rotation.
Refine gray's remaining cap offset at fixed yaw, remove the small wrist tilt with compensating translation, and lower gradually for deeper engagement. Leave the other completed pairs undisturbed.
The gray cap now occupies most of the opening. Remove the small residual offset and apply a short, slow clockwise stroke with only 3 mm descent, staying clear of the wrist limit.
Correct the visible gray shaft offset, then test a smaller tightening stroke with compensating EE translation about the estimated nut center rather than rotating about link6 alone.
Gray's cap is nearly centered. Keep yaw fixed, make a final small correction and controlled descent, then open and lift slightly to verify whether the nut remains seated before resetting the wrist.
Gray now remains seated with the screw cap flush after release. Clear the assembly and unwind the open right wrist toward its home configuration; refine the left arm's origin pose.
All three matching pairs remain visibly seated with both grippers open. Return the right arm smoothly to its origin pose while preserving elbow-up continuity and leaving the assemblies undisturbed.
Refine both origin poses with millimeter-scale corrections, keep the grippers fully open, and allow the arms and seated assemblies to settle.

Red still shows more exposed shaft than yellow, so seating alone may not mean fully tightened. Re-approach red with the open left hand for a careful additional tightening stroke; keep the right arm at origin.
Finish the vertical approach over red and lower the open fingers to just above the nut, preserving its seated alignment before regrasping for tightening.
Center the fingers around the seated red nut, descend only to its side faces, and close without lifting or twisting so its alignment is preserved.
The red nut is centered and remains seated in the closed fingers. Apply a small clockwise tightening stroke with minimal downward feed, checking that the cap stays concentric.
Red remains concentric after the short turn. Continue clockwise with slight center compensation and a small downward feed, keeping ample wrist range for an open-gripper reset.
Red stays seated but has shifted within the fingers. Open and lift slightly, then rewind the empty wrist and re-center above the nut for another controlled tightening stroke without loosening it.
Re-center laterally and close around red's side faces without lifting it. Begin the next clockwise stroke slowly while preserving the seated, concentric alignment.
Red remains centered and seated in the fingers. Continue a controlled clockwise tightening stroke with a small downward feed, leaving ample wrist range and the other pairs undisturbed.
Red stays concentric through the turn. Finish this tightening stroke slowly with minimal descent, stopping well before the wrist limit; keep the right hand open at origin.
Release the seated red nut, lift the open fingers slightly, and unwind the empty wrist for another tightening stroke without turning the nut backward.
Regrasp red at its seated height and apply another clockwise tightening stroke with minimal downward feed. Keep the nut concentric and the right hand open at origin.
Red remains concentric. Finish this clockwise tightening stroke with a very small downward feed, then release without reversing the nut; maintain the right arm at origin.
Red remains seated after the additional tightening and release. Lift the open left hand clear and unwind its empty wrist before returning to origin; leave all three assemblies undisturbed.
Return the open left arm to its origin pose along a smooth elbow-up path. Keep the right arm at origin and avoid disturbing the seated matching pairs.
